speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you tell me how long these nosebleeds and spots on the skin have been happening? Also, has your child had any recent infections, fever, or unusual bruising elsewhere on the body?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any fever, bone pain, or been diagnosed with an infection recently? Also, has there been any bleeding from other sites like the urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Does your child have any history of easy bruising, bleeding after minor injuries, or prolonged bleeding from cuts? I also need to know if there is any family history of bleeding disorders.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the child is attending preschool, so have you observed any other children with similar symptoms recently, or has there been any exposure to sick contacts? Additionally, does the child currently have any fever or appear unusually tired and pale?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, significant weight loss, joint pains, or recent infections.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Coagulation Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special Test (Platelet Function/ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors. Clinical findings include diffuse petechiae on forearms, legs, and trunk; mild gum bleeding; and dried blood at nares. Vital signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 100/60 mmHg, Heart Rate 90 bpm, Respiratory Rate 20 breaths/min.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and coagulation profile but a specific deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors on the platelet surface, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia.
